item.title: 🌊 We build arks for the loudest deniers
item.description: Most of us assume humans occupy a special tier of existence. We believe a biological brilliance separates us from the rest of the animal kingdom, treating this exceptionalism as a hard fact of nature like gravity or oxygen. This belief hides a messy reality: we are often just apes with high-voltage tools, struggling to manage a world our brains never anticipated. We act like drivers who believe they master the road while smoke pours from the engine. We convince ourselves the car keeps moving because of our status rather than a series of lucky accidents. This narrative of superiority masks the structural gaps in our minds and leaves us vulnerable to the same primitive triggers that governed our ancestors in the brush.

item.title: 🎮🧸 Your ego is a game where you are the toy
item.description:
We talk about ego like it is a personality trait. But it is more like a simulation running in the background.

In this simulation:

  • You are the main character.
  • The rules were installed by your family, culture, and past experiences.
  • The rewards and punishments exist mostly in your head.
  • And yet your nervous system reacts as if every round is life or death.

The game mechanics

  1. Your brain builds an internal avatar: “me”.
  2. It tracks a score: approval, status, being right, being admired, being in control.
  3. It predicts moves: “If I say this, post that, achieve this… my score will go up or down.”
  4. It uses real emotional circuitry (pain, shame, pride, anxiety) to enforce the rules.

When you “lose” in this game, get criticised, ignored, rejected, proven wrong, it hurts. Your brain uses some of the same systems involved in physical pain to flag social loss and ego threat.
